title: Rowan Bell · Community Manager · call with Jude Quadstead, Fennel Wheatstead, Edmund Saffronham · September 2026
notice: Synthetic demo material. Invented document; no real meeting, publication, email or call occurred.

blocks.text: Rowan Bell initiated a check-in call with three members of the Timber Verge Repair Co-op network.

They needed a proper door for the new tool shed. The old milling machine from Westgate Foundry’s scrapyard had the right gauge steel. I cut and welded four heavy-duty hinges last week. They’re hung. Door swings smooth.
Rowan noted the completed work and asked Fennel for an update.

My current project is still in the drafting phase. I’m preparing a proposal for the South Copse primary school. The aim is to introduce a basic bicycle maintenance and safety program for the upper-year students. It would cover tire patching, brake adjustments, and road safety principles. I plan to present it to the school council next month.
Rowan asked Edmund about his recent work.

The foundry’s ceramic molds were cracking at a 15% rate due to improper drying. I designed and installed a system of slatted wooden racks in the warm storeroom off the main floor. It allows for consistent air circulation on all sides. Defects have dropped to an estimated 3% in the first week.
That’s a significant improvement. Was the lumber sourced locally?
Rowan closed the call by thanking everyone for their time and updates.
